speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris.

I have noted your recent medication changes and hiking history, but these are less likely causes given the specific combination of cutaneous blisters and painful oral/genital ulcers. Based on this clinical presentation, I am ready to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Direct Immunofluorescence, Indirect Immunofluorescence, Tzanck Smear.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of forearm lesions and oral mucosa.
